prompt:
A premium packaging line is failing intermittently. Root-level observations make the safest-looking action a premature wait or a wrong root cause, unless two deep-leaf facts reach the final decision-maker. Choose the single diagnosis bundle consistent with all observations together.
A: metallic-label glare under low-angle light; handheld scans still work; controller logs stay clean; focus metrics remain stable
B: metallic-label issue from camera focus drift; handheld scans still work; low-angle light worsens misses; focus metrics drift out of tolerance
C: template-refresh miss; matte and metallic labels both fail; handheld scans fail until refresh; logs stay clean
D: conveyor vibration on overweight cartons; label type is irrelevant; handheld scans still work; lowering line speed sharply removes the issue
Return the single best option.

agent_observations.agent_0: Packaging leads know repeated misses alone are not enough to blame optical glare; without a confirming constraint they lean toward a generic wait-and-observe root-cause review.
agent_observations.agent_1: Handheld scans still work, which weakens a template-refresh explanation but does not by itself rule out vibration or focus drift.
agent_observations.agent_2: Miss-rate rises late afternoon when low-angle sunlight enters from the west door, which makes glare plausible but still not decisive.
agent_observations.agent_3: If glare is the cause, the failure should remain label-specific and not disappear entirely when line speed changes a little.
agent_observations.agent_4: Lowering conveyor speed helps slightly, so some operators incorrectly favor vibration even though the improvement is too small to be decisive.
agent_observations.agent_5: Focus calibration metrics visible to maintenance dashboards look normal, but root operators distrust them because they have seen stale focus health before.
agent_observations.agent_6: The line is expensive to pause for optical shielding unless a hard discriminating fact rules vibration and focus drift out.
agent_observations.agent_7: Deep calibration logs confirm focus metrics stayed in tolerance during the exact failing windows, which eliminates the focus-drift bundle.
agent_observations.agent_8: A hidden speed experiment showed the fault persisted on metallic cartons even after carton weight and line speed were normalized, which removes the vibration bundle and leaves only the glare-consistent diagnosis.

prompt:
A customer-merge pipeline must choose one merge policy for a same-day billing run. Root-level operations prefer a broad freeze unless two deep-leaf facts prove a targeted queue is both safe and necessary. Choose the single policy bundle consistent with all observations together.
A: exact-email auto-merge; no manual queue; keeps billing fully live; preserves all profile updates
B: full invoice freeze; manual review of every suspected duplicate; preserves all updates; misses same-day SLA
C: targeted review queue on address plus payment overlap; clear cases stay live; preserves updates; queue stays small
D: targeted review queue on address plus payment overlap; clear cases stay live; newest ambiguous record is deleted to simplify merges
Return the single best option.

agent_observations.agent_0: Without a higher-confidence discriminator than email, operations leaders lean toward a full freeze because they fear duplicate billing more than throughput loss.
agent_observations.agent_1: A same-day SLA exists, but root finance still believes a one-day freeze may be safer if ambiguity remains broad.
agent_observations.agent_2: Address overlap alone is noisy enough that some operators distrust any targeted queue and prefer B.
agent_observations.agent_3: If a reliable second discriminator exists and the ambiguous slice is actually small, then a targeted queue dominates the freeze.
agent_observations.agent_4: Deleting the newest record would simplify review, so D remains tempting unless a deep rule explicitly forbids it.
agent_observations.agent_5: Clear cases can stay live only if the targeted queue really captures most risky pairs; otherwise root keeps leaning back toward B.
agent_observations.agent_6: Loyalty and consent updates are hard to reconstruct if a record is dropped, but root treats that as secondary unless ambiguity scope is proven manageable.
agent_observations.agent_7: Deep payments data shows that address plus payment fingerprint isolates the risky duplicate slice cleanly enough that only a small queue is needed.
agent_observations.agent_8: A buried compliance rule forbids dropping the newest ambiguous profile because it can contain the freshest consent and loyalty state, which rules out D and leaves the small targeted queue as the only safe live policy.

prompt:
A robotics team is selecting a rollout bundle for a navigation patch. Root-level signals make a cautious canary look right, but they do not tell whether rollback must stay armed or whether the deployment should be gated harder. Choose the single bundle consistent with all observations together.
A: global rollout tonight; rollback available; one lidar vendor validated; monitor capacity limited to ten robots
B: canary rollout with rollback enabled; keep rollout gated to validated vendors; collect limited live evidence before broad release
C: canary rollout without rollback; keep rollout gated to validated vendors; collect limited live evidence before broad release
D: revert the planner entirely and collect no new live evidence until every vendor is retested
Return the single best option.

agent_observations.agent_0: Only one lidar vendor has been validated so far, so root leadership already knows a global rollout is too risky and leans toward some form of canary.
agent_observations.agent_1: Support can monitor roughly ten robots, which fits a canary but does not by itself say whether rollback must stay active.
agent_observations.agent_2: Product still wants limited live evidence, so a full revert feels too conservative unless some deeper blocker appears.
agent_observations.agent_3: If rollback is genuinely needed during the canary, then removing it would be a latent but serious mistake rather than a harmless simplification.
agent_observations.agent_4: Dead-end regressions remain unresolved, but root teams still hope they may be rare enough to tolerate under a canary.
agent_observations.agent_5: Several stakeholders argue that disabling rollback simplifies operations and may be acceptable if vendor gating is already strict.
agent_observations.agent_6: The team has some live-traffic appetite, so root does not want D unless evidence shows even a guarded canary is unsafe.
agent_observations.agent_7: Deep simulator audits show the unresolved dead-end regression triggers only on the same validated vendor that would enter the canary, so rollback protection is still necessary during the limited rollout.
agent_observations.agent_8: A buried runbook check confirms the rollback path can revert canaries within minutes without disrupting unrelated robots, which removes the main operational argument for stripping rollback from the canary bundle.

prompt:
An API migration removed a response field still used by downstream analytics. Root-level product pressure makes keeping the migration live without extra compatibility look tempting unless deep-leaf facts overturn that intuition. Choose the single response bundle consistent with all observations together.
A: leave the field removed; accept silent dashboard drift; keep latency gains; no compatibility work
B: fully roll back the migration; restore the old field immediately; lose the latency gains; require no client migration
C: add a compatibility shim with a dated deprecation window; keep latency gains; allow clients to migrate on schedule
D: delete the affected analytics jobs; keep latency gains; rebuild analytics later without a compatibility layer
Return the single best option.

agent_observations.agent_0: Product strongly wants to keep the latency gains, so root teams resist a full rollback and are tempted to keep the field removed if the reporting breakage seems temporary.
agent_observations.agent_1: Silent dashboard drift is disliked, but some operators still think it might be tolerable for a short window if compatibility work is expensive.
agent_observations.agent_2: Deleting the analytics jobs feels cleaner than maintaining compatibility, so D stays superficially alive unless something explicitly rules it out.
agent_observations.agent_3: If compatibility can be added quickly enough, then preserving latency gains no longer conflicts with reporting correctness.
agent_observations.agent_4: A full rollback still feels heavy-handed unless downstream breakage is both important and avoidable.
agent_observations.agent_5: Some leaders doubt client teams will actually migrate on schedule, which weakens enthusiasm for a timed deprecation plan.
agent_observations.agent_6: The migration team fears a shim could become sticky tech debt unless there is evidence the window can stay short and bounded.
agent_observations.agent_7: Deep implementation estimates show the compatibility shim is a one-day change that preserves the new endpoint shape and keeps latency gains, eliminating the main argument for A and D.
agent_observations.agent_8: A buried owner survey shows downstream teams can migrate within two sprints if given a dated cutoff, which makes a bounded compatibility window realistic instead of open-ended.

prompt:
A finance operations team found that one region's tax script rounded invoice totals inconsistently. Choose the best remediation.
A: isolate the affected region, validate a sampled ledger, patch, and reissue with audit trail
B: continue issuing because the error is local to one region
C: remove the tax field from all invoices until the script is rewritten
D: round every invoice upward globally to avoid under-collection
Return the single best option.

agent_observations.agent_0: Sampling shows customer-visible differences above tolerance in only one region, not globally.
agent_observations.agent_1: Regulatory guidance requires a traceable correction path for tax calculation defects.
agent_observations.agent_2: Audit logging for the affected runs is intact, so targeted reissue is feasible.
agent_observations.agent_3: Finance estimates a global pause would be costly and unnecessary because ninety percent of invoices are unaffected.
agent_observations.agent_4: Applying a blanket upward round would create overcharge risk in several tax brackets.

prompt:
An API migration removed a response field still used by downstream analytics jobs.
A: keep the field removed and let dashboards drift until clients catch up
B: delete the downstream analytics job and rebuild it later
C: restore the old endpoint fully and cancel the migration
D: add a compatibility shim with a dated deprecation window and notify owners
Return the single best option.

agent_observations.agent_0: Two downstream jobs still read the field directly and currently write zeros when it is missing.
agent_observations.agent_1: A compatibility shim can be added in about one day without undoing the new API shape.
agent_observations.agent_2: Consumers estimate they can migrate cleanly within two sprints if given a fixed deadline.
agent_observations.agent_3: The new endpoint solves a separate latency problem that stakeholders do not want to lose.
agent_observations.agent_4: Silent dashboard drift is considered higher risk than a short-term compatibility layer.

prompt:
A hospital scheduling tool starts double-booking one specialist after a daylight-saving boundary. Choose the best operational response.
A: leave booking open and let clinic staff resolve conflicts manually in parallel
B: freeze new bookings for that specialist, reconcile, patch timezone handling, then reopen
C: turn off all appointment reminders until the timezone patch is ready
D: remove the specialist from online scheduling permanently
Return the single best option.

agent_observations.agent_0: The issue affects one specialist template immediately after the DST boundary, not the whole clinic.
agent_observations.agent_1: Clinic staff can reconcile existing overlaps in under two hours if new bookings are paused.
agent_observations.agent_2: Continuing to send reminders before reconciliation would notify conflicting patients simultaneously.
agent_observations.agent_3: Timezone patching has already been reproduced in staging with a deterministic failing case.
agent_observations.agent_4: Removing the specialist permanently from online scheduling would create a week-long backlog.

prompt:
A warehouse robot fleet sees one battery model degrading faster than expected during a heat wave. Choose the best fleet policy.
A: increase duty cycle to consume the old batteries quickly before they fail unpredictably
B: suppress thermal alarms to reduce operator noise while monitoring manually
C: shift workloads away from steep hot routes, inspect affected packs, and throttle until replacements arrive
D: randomly swap battery packs between robots to average out the degradation
Return the single best option.

agent_observations.agent_0: Thermal alarms cluster on one battery model and on routes with long ramps near loading bay 4.
agent_observations.agent_1: Replacement stock will arrive in three days, so a short-term throttling policy is feasible.
agent_observations.agent_2: Throughput models show the warehouse can absorb a modest reduction on the hottest routes.
agent_observations.agent_3: Randomly swapping packs would erase degradation history needed for warranty and inspection decisions.
agent_observations.agent_4: Operator logs show the affected robots recover when reassigned to cooler flat routes.
